people.name: Founder
people.title: Founder & Voice of Inner Board
people.mission: Teach. Be the voice. Everything else is someone else's job.
owns: The teaching: the practice, the masterclasses and the podcast's point of view
One weekly Recording Block (about half a day, directed by Clint): 1–2 Becoming You episodes, 7 Rep of the Day videos (30–60 sec each), and any promo or offer videos
One monthly masterclass
One short live session a week in the community group (optional but powerful)
people.invitation: Protect the teaching. Give the team one focused Recording Block a week, and trust them with everything that happens after it.

people.name: Abra
people.title: Chief of Staff & Head of Growth
people.mission: Own the number. Get Inner Board to 1,000 members and protect the founder's time while doing it.
owns: The scorecard: updates it every Friday and runs the Monday leadership meeting from it
Offers and promotions: Founding 1,000 (annual + free hat), Gift the Practice and referrals. Sets the terms, budget and dates
Podcast growth: books Becoming You guests and pitches the founder to other podcasts (our biggest reach lever)
The email list: we don't own a Facebook group's audience, but we own our email list
Partnerships: collaborations, affiliates, and anyone who can bring the practice to a group at once
The founder's calendar: guards the Recording Block
people.invitation: Run the business of Inner Board so the founder can stay focused on teaching. Be the public face for partners and podcast hosts. The job moves from checking that people are on task to owning the growth number.
stop: General check-ins. The scorecard shows who's on track.

people.name: Michelle
people.title: COO & Head of Member Experience
people.mission: Everyone who joins gets everything they paid for, builds a daily rep habit, and stays.
owns: Masterclass production: runs the pipeline and gets the recording and every asset to Logan
Membership assets: replay, workbook, audio drops and slides, complete and live in the app
Onboarding: a new member's first 7 days (welcome, first rep, how to use the app, an invitation to the group)
The community: the Rep of the Day group. Welcomes, keeps the conversation going, moderates, spotlights members
Merch fulfillment: collects addresses, ships the hats, handles issues
Member support: questions about access, billing or content
Logan: sets his priorities and checks his work
people.invitation: Become the member-facing voice next to the founder. Host the monthly New Member Welcome call and a monthly Member Spotlight on the podcast. Be the person members know by name. Mentor Clint rather than approving his work.
stop: Writing status reports. The scorecard replaces both.

people.name: Clint
people.title: Creative Director
people.mission: Make Inner Board look and sound unmistakable everywhere, and turn the founder's weekly recording into a week of content.
people.number: Content shipped per week → group joins
owns: Brand guidelines: one page on colors, fonts, logo use, caption style and voice. Once it exists, routine content goes out without approval
The Recording Block: plans the shot list, sets up, and directs the founder
Podcast production: edits, publishes, cuts 3–5 clips per episode, uploads to YouTube
Rep of the Day: produces and schedules the daily posts 2 weeks ahead
Social: clips, carousels, posting and engagement on our pages
Merch: designs the hat and sweatshirt, runs photo and video shoots in the gear
people.invitation: Own the creative calls: what gets clipped, how it looks, what we try next. Host a short behind-the-scenes series ("how we make Inner Board"). A director, not an editor.
stop: Waiting for approval on routine posts

people.name: Logan
people.title: App Lead
people.mission: The app is where the practice lives. It works, and everything is in it on time.
people.number: Assets live on time; app issues open
owns: Uploads of replays, audio drops, workbooks and Rep of the Day videos
App onboarding screens and the first-7-days flow, built with Michelle
Gift codes and annual plans: the app can sell a gifted year and flags annual sign-ups for the free hat
App numbers for the scorecard each week: active members, sign-ups, annual vs. monthly
people.invitation: Be the person who knows the app inside out, so every asset is live and checked on phone and desktop before anyone has to ask.

tasks.title: Announce the new titles and roles to the team
tasks.notes: Everyone reads their card on the Team page and pushes back on anything that feels wrong.

tasks.title: Set the target date for 1,000 members
tasks.notes: With Abra. The plan assumes 12 months (Nov 30, 2027): about 84 new members a month, or 20 a week. A shorter deadline means a bigger weekly number.

tasks.title: Decide: is the Rep of the Day group free or members-only?
tasks.notes: With Abra. Recommendation: free. The group is the front door; the app is where people go deeper.

tasks.title: Record our baseline numbers in the scorecard
tasks.notes: With Logan. Paid members, annual vs. monthly, email list size, podcast downloads per episode, social followers.

tasks.title: Confirm the annual price and check the hat economics
tasks.notes: Total cost per hat should be under about 15% of the annual price. See Gift the Practice in the Library.

tasks.title: Confirm the app can sell annual plans and gift codes
tasks.notes: It also needs to flag annual sign-ups so we know who gets a hat.

tasks.title: Order hat samples from 2–3 vendors
tasks.notes: With Michelle. Clint owns the design, Michelle the vendors. Samples needed now to order in bulk by Nov 20.

tasks.title: Book a protected weekly Recording Block
tasks.notes: With Clint. Tuesdays, about half a day. Abra guards it on the calendar.

tasks.title: First Recording Block: 2 podcast episodes and 14 Rep of the Day videos
tasks.notes: With Clint. Clint plans the shot list and directs. Wear the gear if samples have arrived.

tasks.title: Create the Rep of the Day Facebook group
tasks.notes: Rules, entry questions (including email) and a welcome post. See Rep of the Day in the Library.

tasks.title: Write the one-page brand guidelines
tasks.notes: Colors, fonts, logo use, caption style and voice. Once it exists, routine posts go out without approval.

tasks.title: Place the bulk hat order (team gets hats and sweatshirts first)
tasks.notes: Hard deadline: hats take 2–4 weeks. Start with about 100–150. If we miss it, run Gift the Practice as "hat ships in January" and say so up front.

tasks.title: Add one call to action to every podcast episode
tasks.notes: With Abra. Default: "Join the free Rep of the Day group."

tasks.title: Soft-launch the group to current members and podcast listeners
tasks.notes: With Clint.

tasks.title: Pitch the founder to 10 podcasts for January and February
tasks.notes: Guest spots are the highest-leverage reach for a lean team. Aim for 2–4 a month.

tasks.title: Create a free lead magnet for email capture
tasks.notes: Promised in the group entry questions along with the 30-Day Rep Challenge. The email list is the audience we own.

tasks.title: Team photo and video shoot in the gear
tasks.notes: This content feeds December and January. Use the samples if the bulk order has not arrived.

tasks.title: Build 7-day onboarding for new members (in the app and by email)
tasks.notes: With Logan. Welcome, first rep, how to use the app, invitation to the group.

tasks.title: Launch Gift a Year: buy the practice for someone, they get a welcome hat
tasks.notes: With Logan (gift codes) and Clint (creative). Podcast call to action for December: "Gift the practice to someone you love."

tasks.title: Team wears the gear in every video, live session and podcast clip
tasks.notes: Everyone. Clint checks it in every shoot.

tasks.title: Ship hats in one weekly batch
tasks.notes: Every Thursday through December. Update hats owed and shipped on Numbers.

tasks.title: Start the weekly founder live session in the group (15–20 min)
tasks.notes: With Clint and Michelle. Fridays. Daily Rep of the Day continues.

tasks.title: December masterclass: "Becoming You in the New Year"
tasks.notes: Michelle runs production. Follow the masterclass pipeline; kick off at Day −7 (Dec 8).

tasks.title: Launch the Founding 1,000 offer: join annually, get a free hat
tasks.notes: Limited to the first 1,000 annual members. Fine print: one per member, shipping region, ship time. Podcast call to action for January.

tasks.title: Start the 30-Day Rep Challenge in the free group
tasks.notes: With Clint (daily content). The big front-door push for the year.

tasks.title: Invite everyone in the challenge to the January masterclass
tasks.notes: With Michelle.

tasks.title: Founder guest podcast appearances begin
tasks.notes: From the pitches sent in November. Target 2–4 a month.

tasks.title: Repost member photos in their hats
tasks.notes: Ongoing through January. Members in the gear are walking invitations.

tasks.title: Launch the "bring a friend" referral program
Start streak rewards: 100 reps earns a sweatshirt
tasks.notes: Tracked by hand at first (members post "Day 100"). Shout-outs at 7, 30 and 100.

tasks.title: Make the monthly masterclass engine run on its own
tasks.notes: Every step of the pipeline has a date and a name, with no reminders needed.

tasks.title: Launch the monthly Member Spotlight podcast segment
tasks.notes: A member's story of becoming. Michelle hosts or co-hosts.

tasks.title: Run the 30- and 90-day retention check and fix the biggest drop-off
tasks.notes: With Logan.

tasks.title: Quarterly review: are we on pace for 1,000?
tasks.notes: Compare the scorecard with the 20-a-week pace and adjust the plan.

content.title: What do you want the next masterclass to cover?
Masterclass is tomorrow — save your spot

We confirm roles, set the target date for 1,000, decide the Rep of the Day group is free, record our baseline numbers, confirm the annual price and gift codes, and order hat samples. Pick who you are and start with your tasks.
